To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we can achieve superior texture classification performance by using a rotationally invariant filter bank, a low dimensional representation of the filter response space (i.e. texton histogram) and a classifier that is trained on the histogram of the training images.
the use of rotationally invariant filters, a low dimensional representation and a statistical approach can lead to superior performance in single image texture classification.

(1) rotationally invariant filters can be used for texture classification from a single uncalibrated image; (2) the use of a low-dimensional filter response space is crucial for good performance; and (3) classification performance is improved when orientation co occurrence statistics are used in the classifier.

the development of an algorithm for texture classification from single, un-calibrated images, which can be used in real world applications.
the development of a robust texture classification method that is applicable to real world images and is based on the statistical analysis of filter responses.
developing a statistical framework for texture classification and the results demonstrate that the proposed approach is effective in classifying a variety of materials.

the use of rotationally invariant filters and a low dimensional representation of the filter response space can be a good alternative to the use of rotation sensitive filters and a higher dimensional filter response space, especially for texture classification.
